title: [Bug] Going until the end of a swiping cycle gives an error
body:
I believe this issue is related to the one I opened about me getting a deletion confirmation for each item to be deleted (#77).

After swiping items until the cycle reset and pressing the "Delete Items" button, the following happens:
1. A popup to confirm the deletion of the first item (I get one for each item as mentioned above);
2. I press allow; then
3. The second popup for the second item shows up; then
4. I press allow; and finally
5. A notification on the bottom of the screen appears saying "No items were deleted"

After this process, and if I go to my file manager, I noticed that only the first item was deleted (the one I first pressed allow) while the rest remained untouched.

A workaround for this is, when I swipe the last item in the cycle, I press the undo button (the arrow) and then press "Delete Items". This does the job for whatever reason.

I'm using an Android 10 phone.

Also tested in an android 11 and 12 phone and this didn't happen.

Bellow is a demonstration of the issue happening. If needed, I can also demonstrate the workaround I described.

title: Didn't detect known 2-3 years old Android Malwares
body:
I was impressed by reading what DivestOS does and then stumbled upon Hypatia. Looked like an awesome much needed App for the less tech savvy people like people from non tech background or Old Parents who wouldn't know what to download or not and might mistakenly download and execute malwares. 

So I thought to give it a try and test. I installed it and updated the databases that are selected by default(all except ClamAV: Main and ClamAV: Daily) and downloaded android malware samples from:

1. [MalwareSamples](https://github.com/MalwareSamples/Android-Malware-Samples)
2. [Maldroid](https://maldroid.github.io/android-malware-samples)
3. Download WhatsApp apk from [apkpure](https://apkpure.com/whatsapp-android/com.whatsapp). It is detected by virustotal by trendmicro. 

Although the realtime scanner was on, none of the above were detected upon download. More interestingly, most of them were years old and already detected and known malwares and shown as detected by ClamAV such as the very first sample on # 2 above under _Easy Samples_. 

Running scan manually from Hypatia App didn't make a difference, neither did updating the remaining two databases make any difference. So I'm wondering if this App is really that helpful. Or am I doing something wrong? Upon little investigating the permissions, I see that Hypatia didn't have/ask for Files permission at all. It only had access to _Photos and Videos_ and _Music and Audio_. Does it work that way?

I'm running latest version of Android 14 on AOSP. No external storage used.

title: Bug: Storage Access (without root)
body:
Hi :wave:,

using Hypatia on Android 11 (Samsung stock version) I noticed that Hypatia seems to be unable to access the device storage.

The granted storage permission reads "Access to media files" in the settings view.

Searching StackOverflow I learned that this might be due to the **"Scoped Storage Policy"** of Android 11.

If I'm not wrong then this will render Hypatia pretty much unusable without root privileges :worried: 

Apparently this can be solved by using the Storage Access Framework ([SAF](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/36862675/android-sd-card-write-permission-using-saf-storage-access-framework)) instead of [`java.io.file`](https://gitlab.com/divested-mobile/hypatia/-/blob/stable/app/src/main/java/us/spotco/malwarescanner/Database.java#L26) for file operations after the user granted access to the device's storage using the directory selector activity of SAF.

I hope someone with more knowledge about SAF, scoped storage access, and android app development in general might have the time to solve this bug. Big thanks in advance!

title: Serialization issue in v0.13.0 (F-Droid / Codeberg Pages) leads to multiple issues [fixed] [release on its way]
body:
# Info

In v.0.13.0 F-Droid / Codeberg Pages, there is a bug within the new serving size feature. It triggers e.g. if:

- Custom food was added or edited to contain an arbitrary serving size
- Possible other occurences as well

The bug can e.g. lead to affected custom food not showing at all anymore and also leads to not showing any serving sizes when searched.

## Background

This is "only" a serialization issue. The underlying data is as safe as always. Because there was a change of the Food.dart and FoodTracked.dart model classes after previously running build_runner locally to generate the toJson() and fromJson() methods, the F-Droid CI pipeline and the Codeberg Pages CI piepline generated different toJson() and fromJson() methods for these classes than checked in in the source code repository.

## Fix

This should be fixed with 1314747232.

## Lookout

Testing, testing, testing. More tests will be implemented in the future. It should also be ensured that generated types do not differ from the check in source code.

Sorry for the inconveniences.

title: USB device disconnect is sporadically  not registered correctly
body:
#### What steps will reproduce the issue?

* Plug in a USB tuner device
* Let it pick up some messages
* Unplug the device
* Observe the notification
* After some time, plug the device back in again
* Observe behavior

#### What behavior did you expect?

Upon unplugging the device, the notification disappears. When I plug it in again, the notification returns and the device starts scanning the FM band and picking up new messages.

#### What behavior are you seeing instead?

Sporadically the notification stays after unplugging the device. When I plug the device back in, the signal strength indicator “flashes” between two states and no messages are received. The logcat show that it is flipping back and forth between two frequencies, which appear to be the start of the band and the last frequency received before the device was first unplugged.

It appears that the old thread which controls and reads from the device never gets killed, and when the device is plugged back in, there are now two competing threads which alternate in sending commands to the device.

#### What version of the software are you using? On what operating system (distribution and version)? Please also indicate related software which may be of importance here.

Several dev versions post-1.2, on LineageOS 14.1

#### Other relevant information

title: Si470x tuner occasionally stuck at 189.8 MHz
body:
Occasionally the tuner appears to be stuck at 189.8 MHz and does not deliver any data.

With the frequency band starting at 87.5 and a channel raster of 0.1, 189.8 corresponds to 0xCFF, the highest value which the  corresponding register can hold, and an out-of-range frequency for any band/channel raster combination. Probes of other registers have also shown all bits to be reported as high, suggesting the same is true for all other registers.

The native Si470x driver included in RDS Surveyor, after which the Android driver was modeled, has also been observed to suffer from this issue. In both cases, the device used a Si4701 chip.

In Qz, unplugging the dongle and plugging it back in had no effect. However, in one instance, unplugging the dongle, killing Qz and plugging the dongle back in got the device to respond normally again.

Similar issues have previously been observed when unplugging the tuner and plugging it back in: the device would remain stuck at 87.5 MHz and not respond to any commands, the only workaround being to kill and restart the process prior to plugging the tuner back in. This was apparently caused by an improperly synchronized shutdown, and the issue went away after properly synchronizing all access methods for the group reader class.

Similar concurrency issues may also be the issue here, which needs to be verified. With all access methods being synchronized, leaking the object from within the constructor may be causing this.

title: No messages read from canned RDS data under certain conditions
body:
#### What steps will reproduce the issue?

* Process a canned RDS data file known to contain TMC data.
* Process another (or the same file again).

#### What behavior did you expect?

TMC messages from both files appear in the GUI (or, if the same file is used twice, the number of updates is increased for each message and the timestamp is updated).

#### What behavior are you seeing instead?

Occasionally, no messages are read on the second attempt. This seems to differ based on the file—some are processed correctly when they are the second file, others are processed correctly as the first file but not as the second.

Analysis (with extra log output inserted) shows that in the case of files not being read, the `DefaultLogMessageVisitor` is never has its `visit(ApplicationChanged)` method called with `AlertC` passed as the new application; currently no idea why.

#### What version of the software are you using? On what operating system (distribution and version)? Please also indicate related software which may be of importance here.

670f6cc, on LineageOS 15.1; the issue seems to have been present all along (also confirmed in 165adb48).

#### Other relevant information

title: Inconsistent message counts in notification and main window
body:
#### What steps will reproduce the issue?

* Prime the cache with canned TMC data which contains cancellation messages.
* Connect to a real tuner and wait to pick up a TMC service.
* Check the message count in the notification and the main app window.

#### What behavior did you expect?

Same number of messages reported in both places.

#### What behavior are you seeing instead?

The notification occasionally reports more messages than the main app window.

#### What version of the software are you using? On what operating system (distribution and version)? Please also indicate related software which may be of importance here.

4ee73163ed0700cb8ee748cb7ae845e5cebe46a1 on LineageOS 15.1.

#### Other relevant information

Looking at the code the reason is obvious: `TmcReceiver`, which generates the notification, simply takes the count from the message cache (which includes messages not visible in the UI, such as cancellations). `MainActivity`, on the other hand, takes the count from the message adapter, which excludes cancellation messages.

**Solving this issue boils down to a design decision: should cancellations be included in the message count or not?**

title: Cancellation messages not sent reliably
body:
#### What steps will reproduce the issue?

With a TraFF consumer app active:
* Receive a message
* Receive a cancellation of that message

#### What behavior did you expect?

Qz sends out the message in TraFF format, then a cancellation message

#### What behavior are you seeing instead?

Even after the cancellation (presumably, see below), Navit still shows a traffic distortion, which is also visible in its message cache. However, neither the Qz GUI nor its TraFF export show that message.

#### What version of the software are you using? On what operating system (distribution and version)? Please also indicate related software which may be of importance here.

a4c979ee, on LineageOS 15.1.

#### Other relevant information

Analyzing RDS logs shows that the message was first received at 14:04 (UTC), last at 14:07. Later RDS logs no longer show a message for this location; a dissection of the RDS data shows a cancellation was received at 14:15:03. A TraFF query at 14:30 no longer reports the message and the Qz GUI no longer showed it. However, the cancellation apparently never got sent via TraFF, which would explain why Navit would still have the stale message.

Logs are attached. The message ID is `tmc:a.1.0:a.1.35925.n.5,24`.

title: Check that pitch/roll tags are not added until the computed values are valid
Correct calculation of yaw pitch and roll tags
body:
# Implement Yaw, Pitch, and Roll Using Accelerometer

## Description
Implement the calculation of **Yaw, Pitch, and Roll** using only the **accelerometer** in the Flutter app.

## Implementation Details
- **Pitch (θ)**: Rotation around the **X-axis**, calculated as:  
  pitch = atan2(ax, sqrt(ay² + az²))
- **Roll (ϕ)**: Rotation around the **Y-axis**, calculated as:  
  roll = atan2(-ay, az)
- **Yaw (ψ)**: **Not directly derivable** from the accelerometer alone, as it requires a reference for horizontal orientation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Correct **Pitch** and **Roll** values derived from accelerometer readings.
- Values provided in **degrees**.
- Smooth and stable motion tracking.

title: Month widget shows "can't show content" on busy months
body:
On a month with many events the month widget fails to render and shows Glance's error layout. Logcat:

```
E/GlanceAppWidget: java.lang.IllegalStateException: There are too many views
    at androidx.glance.appwidget.TranslationContext.nextViewId(RemoteViewsTranslator.kt:176)
```

Reproduced on the emulator with a synced Google account, on 2.22.3's code and on the 2.22.4 branch.

The grid's view count grows with how full the month is (up to 3 lanes per week plus the "+N" row), and `SizeMode.Exact` renders the whole grid once per size the launcher reports. #214 trimmed the views per cell but there is no hard cap on the total, so a busy month goes over Glance's limit.

Fix idea: give the grid a fixed view budget and, when a month would exceed it, fold the lowest lanes into the "+N" count instead of failing. Belongs with the widget overhaul.

title: Month widget arrows die after ~3 taps: oversized RemoteViews kills the widget host
body:
The month widget's prev/next/today arrows work for about two or three taps and
then go dead. They stay dead until the launcher rebinds its widgets — opening the
app or restarting the launcher brings them back for another couple of taps.

It is not the arrows: the tap runs, the state is written, the grid recomposes and
the new month is published. The payload is the problem. The month grid renders as
~740 views, and `SizeMode.Exact` serialises a full copy of it for every size the
host reports (portrait + landscape), so one update is a 450–540 KB `RemoteViews`.

The system pushes that to the launcher over a *oneway* binder call, and a host
process only has a 1 MB async buffer. Two updates fit; the third does not:

```
E/libbinder.IPCThreadState(740): Binder transaction failure. BR_FAILED_REPLY, error: -28 (No space left on device)
E/JavaBinder(740): !!! FAILED BINDER TRANSACTION !!! (parcel size = 536112)
E/AppWidgetServiceImpl(740): Widget host dead: HostId{... pkg:com.google.android.apps.nexuslauncher}
E/AppWidgetServiceImpl(740): android.os.TransactionTooLargeException: data parcel size 536112 bytes
```

`AppWidgetServiceImpl` catches the failure and drops the whole host, so
`host.callbacks` goes null and *every* widget on the home screen stops updating —
ours and other apps' — until the launcher rebinds.

Reproduced on the Android 16 emulator with the 2.19.2 release build.

Fix: keep the published `RemoteViews` small — one composition instead of one per
host size, and stop emitting views the grid does not need.

title: Unnamed calendars fall back to a hardcoded German name
body:
Sibling of #321, split off from that fix because it is not the same shape.

`Fallbacks.UNNAMED_CALENDAR = "(Unbenannter Kalender)"` (`Projections.kt:317`) is a German literal with **no string resource behind it at all** — `event_untitled` at least existed, this has no counterpart in `values/strings.xml`. It is used in two different ways, and they need different treatment:

**Display fallback — the actual bug**

`CalendarMapper.kt:12` substitutes it when a provider row has a null `CALENDAR_DISPLAY_NAME`. That name is then shown in every locale in the calendar list, the calendar picker, per-calendar notification settings, backup and event detail. Same defect as #321: a display string decided in the data layer.

It also leaks into data. `CalendarsScreen.kt:153` prefills the edit sheet with `editing?.displayName`, so opening such a calendar and saving writes the German literal into `CALENDAR_DISPLAY_NAME` for real.

Fix: add a proper string resource, keep `CalendarSource.displayName` blank in the mapper, and substitute in the UI — matching what #321 did for events.

**Write fallback — needs a decision, not a translation**

`CalendarDataSource.kt:379` (`createLocalCalendar`), `:403` (`updateCalendar`) and `:467` (`createManagedCalendar`) do `displayName.trim().ifEmpty { Fallbacks.UNNAMED_CALENDAR }` and put the result into `NAME` + `CALENDAR_DISPLAY_NAME`. That is a **stored** name, so a localised string would freeze whatever language the device had at creation time into the provider — and it would go on to be wrong for the same user after a language change.

`CalendarsScreen.kt:386` already gates the editor on `name.isNotBlank()`, so these are defensive guards that the UI should not be able to reach. Options: reject the empty name at the data layer instead of inventing one, or keep a deliberately locale-independent placeholder and document why it is not translated.

The issue is far more common when it's been a long time since I've checked my feed, so maybe it's somehow related to the other issue? I'm not sure

But basically, sometimes I will open the app and then just see there's a multi-hour gap between the post I was reading and the one that comes after it, with no "Fetch more messages..." separator to grab the posts from the cache. I've checked in the past when talking about this issue with the fedliab account on fedi itself, and the posts *are* populating in the cache, it's just that there's no way for me to retrieve them without that part of the UI showing up

also, thank you for all your work on fedilab over the years! I appreciate it a lot

body:
First I was euphoric since I was able to reproduce the bug, but then my script to prepare Fedilab for scheduled boosts closed and reopened the app cleanly, and now it is difficult to reproduce it in a test timeline. Still, the video shows the problem well.

Description for the video:

1. Create an art timeline containing a Japanese hashtag (for example, cat `猫`).
2. Load the timeline and go to its end by clicking it while it is open.
3. Pull to refresh (better: have the `load all timelines` setting enabled, switch to another timeline, then pull to refresh).
4. Older content is now added to the timeline. Clearing cache or quitting Fedilab won't fix it.
5. Click the timeline to reset it.

<video src="/attachments/16b40385-2ba6-4a0f-958a-393a4bcdd9f5" title="Screen_Recording_20260628_195051_Fedilab-ezgif.com-resize-video" controls></video>

Since I wasn't able to instantly reproduce it after a clean app restart, I will explain how I can trigger it in my "problem timeline".

1. Clear the cache.
2. Load the "problem timeline".
3. Quit Fedilab and reopen it, or trigger a refresh by changing timelines.
4. Load the "problem timeline".
5. Older content is loaded.

Properties of the "problem timeline":

- Five hashtags, to see whether my server changes the existing limit (4 hashtags).
- One Japanese hashtag.
- Many posts with multiple pictures.
- Some posts in there are from me. They are very often loaded when the bug occurs, often in a block (4 posts from me that were posted over a timespan of more than a week).

I wish it were definitively the Japanese hashtag, but sadly the bug report became vague after the app was restarted by my script. ☹️ Still, as you can see in the video, there is something wrong.

title: MCP client (SSE mode) posts to a malformed messages endpoint — duplicates the server path
body:
When connecting to a self-hosted MCP server (n8n's MCP Trigger node, which uses the legacy HTTP+SSE transport), the SSE handshake opens successfully, but Wristotle's follow-up POST to the messages endpoint uses a malformed URL that duplicates the server's path segment — resulting in a 404.

Setup

MCP server: n8n MCP Trigger node, path wristotle-reminders
Correct server URL: https://n8n.gadgeteer.co.za/mcp/wristotle-reminders/sse
Wristotle MCP server transport setting: SSE

Steps to reproduce

Add an MCP server in Wristotle: Settings → MCP servers → add https://n8n.gadgeteer.co.za/mcp/wristotle-reminders/sse
Set transport to SSE (Streamable HTTP, the default, fails differently — see "Also observed" below)
Trigger a connection (e.g. tap refresh on the server card, or invoke ask agent with a query that would need the tool)

Expected

Wristotle opens the SSE stream (GET), receives the server's endpoint event containing the correct messages URL, and POSTs subsequent MCP protocol messages to that URL.

Actual

Wristotle POSTs to:

https://n8n.gadgeteer.co.za/mcp/wristotle-reminders/mcp/wristotle-reminders/messages

Note wristotle-reminders and the /mcp/ segment both appear twice — it looks like the client is concatenating the full base URL (including path) with a relative messages path from the server, rather than resolving the server-provided endpoint URL directly (or a relative URL correctly against the original base).

n8n correctly returns a 404 for this malformed path:

json
{"code":404,"message":"The requested webhook \"POST wristotle-reminders/mcp/wristotle-reminders/messages\" is not registered."}

Full error shown in-app:

Failed: Error connecting to transport: Error POSTing to endpoint (HTTP 404): {"code":404,"message":"The requested webhook \"POST wristotle-reminders/mcp/wristotle-reminders/messages\" is not registered.","hint":"The workflow must be active for a production URL to run successfully..."}

Also observed (Streamable HTTP, default transport)

Before switching to SSE, with the default "Streaming-HTTP-by-default" transport, connecting to the same URL produced:

Failed: streamable HTTP error, code 404. message: This webhook is not registered for POST requests. Did you mean to make a GET request?

This is consistent with Wristotle POSTing directly to the /sse endpoint (which only accepts GET to open the stream) before falling back — so both the default transport and the SSE fallback fail against this server, for different reasons.

Environment

Wristotle companion: v1.16.0
Watch: Pebble Time 2
MCP server: n8n (self-hosted), MCP Trigger node, "HTTP+SSE" style endpoint (URL ends in /sse)

Impact

Any self-hosted MCP server that exposes the legacy SSE transport (n8n's built-in MCP Trigger node being one common example) can't currently be connected to Wristotle — both the default and SSE-fallback transport paths fail before any tool call can be made.

title: Feature Request: Highlight Noted Cells in Other Color
body:
## Motivation

I am not fond of the "Highlight Equal Values Only" option, as it makes the grid difficult to parse, but I miss notes often with the "Highlight Full Cell" setting

### Proposal

1. "Highlight Full Cell" mode should use the "Pencil Mark Background" color instead of the Filled Background
2. Optionally, this can be a toggle such that the highlight mode setting would read:
   - Highlight Equal Values Only
   - Highlight Full Cell with Note Color
   - Highlight Full Cell with Fill Color
   - Disabled

title: Huawei MediaPad 5 lite (Android 9) : UI color problem
body:
## Problem description

In version 4.5.0 some user interface colors are set in a way that makes it almost impossible to ready any text. Game colors are okay.

I show the effect in an embedded picture.

## System information

* **Open Sudoku version**: _4.5.0_
* **Android version**: _9_
* **Device info**: _Huawei MediaPad 5.0 lite_

## Additional notes

Example (Screenshot): Note that the puzzle list cannot be read, since there are black letters on black background. Changing the color scheme does not make any difference and there are no possibilities to set colors in the tablet configuration.

![Screenshot_20251007_174901_org.moire.opensudoku.jpg](/uploads/d9dc2f273dc91aceffbf7840e0afdedd/Screenshot_20251007_174901_org.moire.opensudoku.jpg)

title: Keypad not correctly displayed
body:
## Problem description

In portrait mode on the Lenovo tablet, the keys are displayed with a gap. 

In landscape mode, the keys on the keypad are shifted.

This issue has occurred since updating com.google.android.material:material to v1.13.0.

### Steps to reproduce

The landscape problem can be reproduced with the emulator and device "Pixel Tablet"

title: PuzzleListFilter is show as pointer and not as text
body:
In the development version the display of the puzzle filter list is shown as pointer and not as text.

It seems that the "class PuzzleListFilter(context: Context)" was changed ...

You can reproduce the fault by setting a filter for the puzzle list and check the text in the status bar.

title: incorrectly highlighted cells
body:
## Problem description

When eliminating a candidate with "Highlight same value cells" turned on, the cell remained highlighted for that candidate. 3-4 other cells as I progressed through the puzzle also remained highlighted when they shouldn't be.

<details><summary>Screenshot</summary>
![Screenshot_20250405-154031__1_](/uploads/eff03d22c472eafa1090c107f6632c04/Screenshot_20250405-154031__1_.png)
</details>

### Steps to reproduce

Could not reliably reproduce, but this is how it happened:
* go to elimate candidate-9 from R4C3 but accidentally enter 9 as answer (was not in candidate mode)
* hit undo
* accidentally hit wrong button and eliminate the wrong candidate
* hit undo
* eliminate candidate-9 from R4C3 and R6C3
* noticed that R4C3 was still highlighted (see screenshot). R6C3 was correct.

### Steps to try to resolve

* hit undo back to previous step and redo - still highlighted
* erase R4C3 and reenter numbers - still highlighted
* turn off "highlight same value cells" and turn on again - still highlighted
* additionally, a few more cells (different numbers) exhibited the same issue as I continued
* putting the final answer in a cell stopped it from being highlighted for the wrong candidate number

## System information

* **Open Sudoku version**: 4.4.4
* **Android version**: 13
* **Device info**: motorola "moto g stylus 5g (2022)"

title: Unavoidable cheating...
body:

title: Repeatedly fails to download apps on slightly subpar internet
body:
I've only used F-Droid a little here and there, and G-Droid even less, but I definitely like G-Droid a LOT better for many reasons. There are several issues I've noticed with it, though (many are common with, though sometimes slightly different from, F-Droid). Anyways, I apologize for the "spam" from posting them all; I've been told in the past I shouldn't post multiple issues, but I've also been told I should split them up instead of posting one with multiple topics, so there's apparently no winning.

This issue relates to how it handles downloads with a sketchy connection. It keeps failing when trying to install or update apps, just like F-Droid. Unlike F-Droid, when it happens, it simply stops trying, whereas F-Droid at least pops up an error message, though that message is misleading since it says the apk can't be found, when the actual problem seems to be due to my internet setup and is definitely NOT an issue with the apk not being present. I know this because after I tried installing an app with F-Droid a couple times, I tried with G-Droid and it succeeded, which at first I thought meant G-Droid didn't suffer from the same problem as F-Droid and the Play Store, but I now see it just succeeded by chance and it does in fact have the same problem. I'm currently accessing the internet on my phone through a PDANet hotspot on my computer, which gets its internet from a PDANet hotspot on a second phone. I'm going through the computer for two reasons: the distance between the phones is too great, making the signal between them weak and unstable, and if I connect directly to the phone Android thinks there's no internet (the Wi-Fi icon has an x on it and it says no internet connection), whereas going through the computer is sees the internet. From what I can tell, when Android thinks there's no internet, even when there is, the Play Store won't download apps/updates. However, even though it does work with the current setup, it still seems problematic, as downloads always freeze for anywhere from a few seconds to a few minutes partway through, especially when they get to 97-99%. I was hoping F/G-Droid would do better, but it seems they do not, and are actually worse, since they more often than not will just fail (though the Play Store does a lot, too, and I'll often have to tell it to download an update multiple times before it will finally work, just as I'm experiencing with F/G-Droid). It also sometimes takes me a few tries to get a site to load, so just like how web browsers just give up instead of continuing to attempt to download the site data (which I find to be an irritatingly horrible design), so too do the various market apps apparently. I've also noticed that every time I try to upgrade an app, the storage use of G-Droid creeps up (~0.04MB each time, which really adds up when I have to keep trying over and over). This is all in user data; cache remains the same. All of this said, while the connection does tend to drop from time to time, it's certainly stable enough that apps should be able to be downloaded without this much trouble.

title: Change of default gateway doesn't work
body:
*Created by: yvesf*

reported by _s4dsniper_ (Thanks!)

It seems you don't change the default gateway after DNS tunnel is ready so,
the only thing you can reach is the iodine server (via IP). If I launch my
browser and try to reach a website : nothing load.

But if you do (in Terminad Emulator):

```
# busybox route del default
# busybox route add default gw 172.16.0.1 (iodine server IP)
```

web is working, even if very slow (as expected)

So maybe I'm missing something but shouldn't AndIodine change the default
gateway to route all traffic in the DNS tunnel ?

title: Incorrect display of some emoji when forced to basic variant
body:
### Detailed description

I'd noticed a [bug in the Mastodon web client regarding emoji and `U+FE0E VARIATION SELECTOR 15`](https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/issues/26089#issuecomment-5458991880) in which, when displaying a posting (but not when editing it), the variation selector is disregarded.

Thus, `😆` (U+1F606; default colour emoji variant) is displayed correctly but `😆︎` (U+1F606 U+FE0E; basic variant) is also displayed as the colour variant, as if the selector wasn't there.

(Yes, I'd deliberately typed this: custom X11 compose sequences FTW.)

Tusky shows the same problem, but it does so in both display and editing contexts.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Privately post the following text to yourself (using a web client) then view it via Tusky:

`default: 😆  basic: 😆︎ – latter should look different`

### Debug information

Tusky 32.2
Android 16
Motorola g35
Probably any Mastodon server (tested on 3.7 and a 3.8 glitch-soc snapshot)

title: Login WebView hangs on OAuth pages that require DOM storage (domStorageEnabled never set)
body:
### Detailed description

The in-app login WebView (LoginWebViewActivity) enables JavaScript but never enables DOM storage (webView.settings.domStorageEnabled, which defaults to false). On servers whose /oauth/authorize page is a JavaScript SPA that reads localStorage during bootstrap, the page never finishes loading - the user sees the instance logo and a spinner forever, and never reaches the login form.

Root cause
In app/src/main/java/com/keylesspalace/tusky/components/login/LoginWebViewActivity.kt, the WebView settings block (around lines 137-144) sets javaScriptEnabled = true but never sets domStorageEnabled = true. With DOM storage off, localStorage access in the authorize page's bootstrap throws/returns null and the SPA fails to mount.

Suggested fix
webView.settings.domStorageEnabled = true
Mastodon's own /oauth/authorize is server-rendered HTML and needs no storage, which is why this has gone unnoticed; SPA-based authorize pages (Misskey/Sharkey family) need it.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Add an account on a server whose OAuth authorize page is an SPA needing localStorage.
2. Enter the domain, tap the login button (in-app WebView path).
The WebView shows the instance logo + spinner and never renders the login/consent form.

Workaround
The "Login with browser" option (overflow menu) works, because the CustomTab has DOM storage enabled.

### Debug information

Tusky 32.2
Android 13
Xiaomi Note 10 Pro
dev.electricrequiem.com

title: Counter skips days, incorrect prediction
body:
Thank you for maintaining this great application. Great work!

Version info: Periodical 1.71; Android 13

In a recent cycle, I noticed that the counter of the priod length was suddenly counting increments of two. See screenshot:
![image](https://github.com/arnowelzel/periodical/assets/86455551/5fa0f10a-3ea1-4af0-a6a4-c30374708813)

Removing the 11th and marking it again as start of the cycle, restores normal behaviour:
![image](https://github.com/arnowelzel/periodical/assets/86455551/7bf9a30a-dfbc-419d-8f57-aafb09d73f35)

I could not reproduce this, however I have backups of the DB before and after the Re-adding of the 11th, which I can provide as PM if needed.

This bug was the source of some confusion, since the user expects those counters to work correctly (the human eye won't even notice at first glance). The next cycle is "silently" predicted 3 days earlier, so you are supposedly too late...

title: Adding a new period day with intensity "1" causes strange effects
body:
Steps to reproduce:

- add details without a period on a blank day after the last period
- select a day after this day and open detail view
- set period to "yes"
- change intensity from "2" to "1"
- go back to the calendar

Result:

All days between the last period and the selected day appear as "blank" and the day after the selected day is marked as period.

The list will also not show the new day as period.

Expected result:

There is a new period starting with intensity 1.

title: Detailed content description for labels missing in some cases
body: The calendar view contains two tables to make the "fling" effect possible. Unfortunately, in one of those tables the detailed content description for the day label at the top of the table is missing, so screen readers will only announce "mo", "tu" and so on.

title: Crashes on sync on Android 14
body:
After allowing access to the nextcloud account, the app crashes:

```
AndroidRuntime  D  Shutting down VM
E  FATAL EXCEPTION: main
E  Process: de.micmun.android.nextcloudcookbook, PID: 29919
E  java.lang.RuntimeException: Unable to start service de.micmun.android.nextcloudcookbook.services.sync.SyncService@318ec4a with Intent { cmp=de.micmun.android.nextcloudcookbook/.services.sync.SyncService }: android.app.MissingForegroundServiceTypeException: Starting FGS without a type  callerApp=ProcessRecord{daccef6 29919:de.micmun.android.nextcloudcookbook/u0a682} targetSDK=34
E      at android.app.ActivityThread.handleServiceArgs(ActivityThread.java:5286)
E      at android.app.ActivityThread.-$$Nest$mhandleServiceArgs(Unknown Source:0)
E      at android.app.ActivityThread$H.handleMessage(ActivityThread.java:2531)

E      at com.android.internal.os.RuntimeInit$MethodAndArgsCaller.run(RuntimeInit.java:608)
E      at com.android.internal.os.ZygoteInit.main(ZygoteInit.java:1103)
E  Caused by: android.app.MissingForegroundServiceTypeException: Starting FGS without a type  callerApp=ProcessRecord{daccef6 29919:de.micmun.android.nextcloudcookbook/u0a682} targetSDK=34
E      at android.app.MissingForegroundServiceTypeException$1.createFromParcel(MissingForegroundServiceTypeException.java:53)
E      at android.app.MissingForegroundServiceTypeException$1.createFromParcel(MissingForegroundServiceTypeException.java:49)
E      at android.os.Parcel.readParcelableInternal(Parcel.java:4882)
E      at android.os.Parcel.readParcelable(Parcel.java:4864)
E      at android.os.Parcel.createExceptionOrNull(Parcel.java:3064)
E      at android.os.Parcel.createException(Parcel.java:3053)
E      at android.os.Parcel.readException(Parcel.java:3036)
E      at android.os.Parcel.readException(Parcel.java:2978)
E      at android.app.IActivityManager$Stub$Proxy.setServiceForeground(IActivityManager.java:7214)
E      at android.app.Service.startForeground(Service.java:775)
E      at de.micmun.android.nextcloudcookbook.services.sync.SyncService.onStartCommand(SourceFile:172)
E      at android.app.ActivityThread.handleServiceArgs(ActivityThread.java:5268)
E      ... 9 more
```

Seems to be caused by missing permission for foreground services: https://developer.android.com/about/versions/14/changes/fgs-types-required#permission-for-fgs-type

The following patch fixes the crash:

```patch
diff --git a/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml b/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml
index 503fc31..089bbb7 100644
--- a/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml
+++ b/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml
@@ -15,6 +15,9 @@
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.VIBRATE" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED" />
+   <uses-permission
+      android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC"
+      android:minSdkVersion="34" />

<application
android:name=".MainApplication"
@@ -58,7 +61,8 @@
<service
android:name=".services.sync.SyncService"
android:enabled="true"
-         android:exported="false" />
+         android:exported="false"
+         android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" />

<receiver
android:name=".services.RemainReceiver"
diff --git a/app/src/main/java/de/micmun/android/nextcloudcookbook/services/sync/SyncService.kt b/app/src/main/java/de/micmun/android/nextcloudcookbook/services/sync/SyncService.kt
index 12ea0dc..003824c 100644
--- a/app/src/main/java/de/micmun/android/nextcloudcookbook/services/sync/SyncService.kt
+++ b/app/src/main/java/de/micmun/android/nextcloudcookbook/services/sync/SyncService.kt
@@ -5,6 +5,7 @@ import android.app.IntentService
import android.app.PendingIntent
import android.content.Context
import android.content.Intent
+import android.content.pm.ServiceInfo
import android.os.Build
import android.os.IBinder
import android.util.Log
@@ -98,7 +99,11 @@ class SyncService : IntentService("SyncService") {

NotificationChannelManager.createSyncServiceNotificationChannel(this)
val serviceNotification = NotificationChannelManager.createSyncServiceNotification(this)
-      startForeground(SYNC_SERVICE_NOTIFICATION_ID, serviceNotification.build())
+      if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU) {
+         startForeground(SYNC_SERVICE_NOTIFICATION_ID, serviceNotification.build())
+      } else {
+         startForeground(SYNC_SERVICE_NOTIFICATION_ID, serviceNotification.build(), ServiceInfo.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_DATA_SYNC)
+      }
sync()
return START_STICKY
}
```

Not opening a PR, since even with this fix, I can't get it to sync  - getRecipes gets stuck after `mApi.performNetworkRequestV2(nextcloudRequest)` without doing anything else. Not sure if it needs more changes for Android 14, or if it's something with my Nextcloud instance.

title: latin1 support (metatags)
body:
I'm using french accents and characters. In recent systems, the default encoding is UTF-8. In French, we used to use latin1 with some accents.
According to the [ID3 wikipedia page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ID3), both seems to be classical encodings for mp3 metadata.

I can still find latin1 it in a many of my files, such as in [this example](http://jmtrivial.info/divers/audio2.zip) where the title contains characters "«" and "»" around "2", or where the second track has the following title: "Il n'est pas facile d'être maman" (accent in the "e"). 

Using `mid3v2` from Mutagen, this encoding can be identified (`mid3v2 --list-raw "$file"`). On many applications such as vlc on android, or almost any software on GNU/Linux, these characters are correctly interpreted.

However in SMP, this latin1 encoding seems to be not correctly handled on a few number of files (such as the ones in the archive), especially when two latin1 characters are matching an utf8 encoding.

title: Design inconsistencies and usability issues
body:
### Usability issues and bugs
- [ ] When I open the app for the first time, it has a empty screen without any tabs, it should be the same screen as usual, just that instead of the graph, the page should be empty, everything else such as tabs etc should be there
- [ ] When I open the app for the first time, I can only add glucose reading, the fab should be same as normal fab (see previous point)
- [x] When I am in history tab, and I add a reading, I'm taken to the overview tab. I should stay in the same tab where I was previously
- [x] Scroll should be enabled in "Add reading" activities
- [ ] The back button in the "A1C calculator" neither dismisses the keyboard, nor goes back, it should go back
- [ ] In the "Assistant", I can slide things out, but it's not immediately obvious what happened (I was confused at first), I usually expect to see something like what Gmail shows you, or a snackbar saying "Archived the tip" and "Undo" button.
- [ ] When you're scrolling back up in assistant, and have no archived tips, you see a gray area at the bottom, which usually has the archived button, it should have the button instead of being a gray area, the archived view can just say no archived tips
- [ ] Clicking on Archived button should slide it up instead of a sudden transition, I think easiest way is to go to another activity with a proper back button and title
- [ ] You can slide things in the archived view to restore them, which I don't think a well known pattern, I first thought I deleted it. It shouldn't get restored on slide. When I tap on it, it should show an action sheet with the restore menu
- [ ] When you tap on things in assistant, it should show a action sheet with "Archive" option
- [ ] Scrolling up doesn't hide the tab bar once I open and close the archived view
- [ ] If I scroll up and hide the appbar in one tab, I can't bring it back in other tabs
- [ ] Tapping on an item in "History" should show an action sheet with the "Delete" and "Edit" options (we don't need a long press here unless we add a detail screen)
- [ ] When I click on "send feedback" to open Gmail compose dialog, pressing back doesn't take me back to the app, are we adding NEW_TASK or something?
- [ ] In settings, or wherever we have switches the label should read like "Turn **FreeStyle Libre support** on"
- [ ] When I delete an item from history, it fades out and takes too long to be removed (I can long press again within this time). It should vertically shrink, and within 200ms, and disable any interactions.
- [ ] The save button is consistent across activities. We should have the text "SAVE" with a checkmark icon on the appbar when we're saving something, instead of a "FAB"
- [ ] There's no extra spacing at the bottom of overview and history screens, so the FAB might cover things
### Text
- [x] In the "Backup & Export" dialog, the title should say "Backup & export" instead of "Google Drive Backup"
- [x] In the "Backup & Export" dialog, "CSV export" should be called "Export to CSV file"
### Visual
- [x] Font is not Lato in tabs, FAB labels, all "Add reading" activities
- [ ] Lots of screens are grey, here is what they should be - if they are empty - grey, if they're list background - grey, in all other cases, background should be white
- [x] In assistant, the title of the tips should be bold and darker
- [ ] In settings, the subtitle should be smaller, and both title and subtitle should have 1.5 line height so that they don't look congested, 
- [ ] Buttons in the items in the assistant, or any other places don't feel like buttons, they should be 32dp high, with 13pt semibold label, and 16dp horizontal padding
- [ ] Some activities have white back button, and some have faded black, all activities should have white back button
- [x] The FAB is placed way higher than the guidelines suggest, should be 16dp from right and 16dp from bottom
- [ ] The FAB should've the same elevation as the appbar
- [ ] In the "A1C calculator", the appbar elevation seems different, it should be same as other screens
- [ ] The caret thickness should be more (same thickness as normal inputs)
- [x] The icon for "Backup & Export" in drawer should be "backup"
- [x] The color of the icons in the navigation drawer should be "#757575"
- [x] The text in navigation drawer should be bold/semibold
- [ ] Separators are too thick, they should be 1pixel (physical pixel) thick and "#eee"

title: [Bug] Program loop at start repeats each exercise instead of the whole sequence
body:
### What happened?

If a program begins with a loop block, the app repeats each exercise inside the loop individually instead of repeating the entire sequence.
- For example, a program defined as: 
    - loop x2
        - A
        - B
        - C 
    - end loop 

should produce: A B C A B C — but instead produces: A A B B C C.  If there is at least one exercise before the loop, the loop repeats correctly.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a program that starts with a loop containing multiple exercises.
2. Start the program.
3. Observe that each exercise inside the loop repeats consecutively (A A B B C C) rather than the whole sequence repeating (A B C A B C).

**Expected behavior**

A loop should repeat the entire sequence of exercises inside it, producing ABCABC for loop x2 in the example.

### App version

1.22.0

### Device / Android version

Android 16 (Pixel 6)

title: [Bug]  CSV import does not support RFC 4180 quoted fields (breaks exercise names with commas)
body:
### What happened?

Importing a CSV file containing exercise names with commas (e.g. Feet-Assisted Hang (18mm, Half-Crimp)) fails with "Exercise not found" for every affected row. The import parser uses line.split(",") which treats commas inside quoted fields as column delimiters.

For example, the CSV line:

"Feet-Assisted Hang (18mm, Half-Crimp)" gets split into:

- "Feet-Assisted Hang (18mm"
-  Half-Crimp)"

instead of the intended first column being Feet-Assisted Hang (18mm, Half-Crimp) (with the enclosing " removed and the inner comma treated as literal data).

The exercise lookup then searches for "Feet-Assisted Hang (18mm instead of Feet-Assisted Hang (18mm, Half-Crimp) and fails. This happens with any field value containing a comma — exercise names, comments, etc. The CSV file itself is valid RFC 4180 (fields with commas are wrapped in double quotes), but the parser ignores the quoting entirely.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an exercise with a comma in its name, e.g. Feet-Assisted Hang (18mm, Half-Crimp)
2. Go to export, export a Records CSV
3. Try to re-import that same CSV
4. The import fails with "Exercise not found" for all rows referencing that exercise

### App version

1.22.0

### Device / Android version

Google Pixel 6

title: [Bug] Rotation causes app to lose state and return to main menu
body:
### What happened?

When the device is rotated (portrait ↔ landscape), the app immediately loses its current navigation state and returns to the main menu, regardless of which screen the user is currently on. This affects all screens in the app, not just workout sessions.

**Expected Behavior:**

- App should either:

    -  **Graceful rotation handling** - App adapts to landscape/portrait seamlessly
    -  **Ignore rotation** - App locks to portrait to prevent issues

  
**Actual Behavior:**

- App loses all navigation state and returns to main menu
- User loses their place in the app navigation
- Any unsaved work or progress may be lost

**Additional Information:**

This issue occurs on every screen in the app, not just during workouts. Users cannot rotate their device for better viewing without losing their navigation state. The problem is most noticeable during workout sessions where progress is lost, but it affects the entire app experience.

**Root Cause Analysis:**

The navigation state is managed using remember { mutableStateOf<Screen> } which doesn't persist across activity recreations caused by configuration changes (rotation). The MainActivity doesn't implement onSaveInstanceState/onRestoreInstanceState to preserve navigation state.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the app and navigate to any screen (Settings, Exercise List, Record, Workout, Program execution, etc.)
2. Rotate the device (portrait ↔ landscape)
3. Observe that the app immediately returns to the main menu

### App version

<= 1.16.0

### Device / Android version

Google Pixel 6 / Graphene OS (Compilation Number: 2026011301, Android Version: 16)

title: Nombre de tickets non actualisé après en avoir jeté
body:
Hello !

Signalement d'un petit bug d'affichage : lorsque l'on jette un ticket, le nombre total de tickets en haut de l'écran n'est pas actualisé. Il faut changer d'onglet et revenir pour que celui-ci soit actualisé.

Exemple :

- Je jette un ticket jaune alors que j'avais 164 tickets, dont 25 jaunes (voir capture 1).

![image](/uploads/83ab91f083bde79c9d7781a6f7befe45/image.png){width="269" height="600"}

- Le nombre de tickets jaunes est bien actualisé (24) mais pas le nombre total de tickets (toujours 164 au lieu de 163, voir capture 2).

![image.png](/uploads/2345425881bbdcad75c96310c545846e/image.png){width=269 height=600}

- Si je change d'onglet et que je reviens aux tickets, cette fois le nombre total de tickets est actualisé (163) ; le nombre de tickets de chaque couleur est pourtant resté identique.

![image.png](/uploads/7dfa9d370dd31155936957263df5a925/image.png){width=269 height=600}

J'espère que ce signalement pourra être utile.

Bonne journée !

title: L’application se ferme automatiquement (crash) à proximité de certaines gares
body:
## Comportement observé

Lorsque nous approchons certaines gares, l’application se ferme systématiquement : la gare n'a pas le temps de s’afficher et il est impossible de tamponner.

## Informations additionnelles

Ce problème a été reproduit sur deux appareils distincts, aux mêmes moments et aux mêmes endroits (nous voyageons en couple).

**Liste des gares où cela a été observé jusqu'ici :**

* Paris Gare-du-Nord (nous y passons souvent sans avoir jamais pu tamponner)
* La Chapelle
* Barbes Rochechouard
* Paris Montparnasse
* Bordeau Saint Jean (nous sommes passés deux fois)
* Agen (nous sommes passés deux fois)

**Gares où tout a fonctionné normalement alors qu’on pensait y rencontrer le bug**

* Saint-Lazare

## Hypothèses

* Il semble que le crash ait lieu lorsque l'appli détecte notre position dans les gares listées ci-dessus.
  * Autrement dit, nous avons l'impression que l'appli acquiert notre position, souhaite nous montrer les gares à proximité, puis plante
* Le problème survient-il uniquement dans certaines grandes gares ?
* Peut-être que l’application tente d’afficher (ou récupérer) trop de données d’un coup ?

## Version de l'application

1.5.7 pour les deux appareils

---

Si certains utilisateurs ont ou n’ont pas ces problèmes dans les gares listées, leurs retours pourraient être utiles.

Faites moi savoir si vous avez besoin de plus d'informations ! Je peux essayer d'enregistrer mon écran la prochaine fois qu'on est à Gare-du-Nord, si ça peut aider.

title: Autodiscovery never reaches mail./jmap. when the apex well-known hangs
body:
Related: #137 (SRV declined; well-known + guessed subdomains is the path), #209 (relative session URLs; 1.5.6 confirmed on real Cyrus).

Leave the server field empty. Sterna probes `autodiscoverHosts`: the email domain first, then `mail.`, `jmap.`, `api.` (`Jmap.kt`). Rank 0 is probed alone; later ranks wait until it settles. The whole search has a 10s budget (`JMAP_DISCOVERY_BUDGET_MS`).

On a Cyrus setup the JMAP session is on `mail.example.com` (and `_jmap._tcp` points there). The apex `https://example.com/.well-known/jmap` does not 404 — TCP to :443 never completes. Rank 0 hangs until the budget dies, so `mail.example.com` is never asked. Typing `mail.example.com` (or the session URL) works.

Expected: a connect timeout on rank 0 should count as `NoAnswer` quickly enough that `mail.`/`jmap.`/`api.` still run inside the budget. A blackholed apex should not hide a host already on the list.

Not asking to reverse the #137 SRV decision.

title: Opening uncached IMAP messages is very slow
body:
### Environment

- Sterna 1.4.8 (168)
- OnePlus Ace 3V (PJF110)
- Android 16 / crDroid 16.0, build `BP4A.251205.006`
- Microsoft Outlook account over IMAP

### Problem

Opening an email often feels extremely slow, even though the inbox and the rest of the app are responsive. The message body eventually appears; this is not the empty-body failure reported in #154.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Sterna and wait for the inbox to settle.
2. Open an IMAP message whose body is not already cached (for example, one not opened since installing/updating 1.4.8).
3. Observe the delay before the message body is visible.

### Device-side observations

- A cold launch of the main activity took about 307 ms, so app startup itself is fast.
- The local databases total only about 1.3 MB.
- UI frame statistics for the inbox were normal (under 1% jank in the sample).
- While Sterna was in the foreground, one sampled IMAP socket to the Microsoft endpoint on port 993 was in `CLOSE-WAIT`. This was only one observation, not proof of the root cause, but it may indicate a stale pooled connection adding a failed attempt/reconnect before the fetch.

### Relevant source paths

The current source appears to make an uncached IMAP open fully synchronous:

- `MailRepository.openEmailImap()` calls `imap.fetchSource()`, which fetches the full raw source and then parses MIME.
- `ImapMailService.fetchSource()` calls `onMailbox()` without a finite budget; the default session budget is 0.
- `prefetchInboxBodies()` immediately returns for IMAP, so recent IMAP bodies are not prefetched.
- `BODY_CACHE_PURGE_VERSION = 168`, so 1.4.8 intentionally invalidates the previous body cache once. This makes the lack of IMAP body prefetch especially visible after that update.
- `MessageScreen` keeps the WebView at alpha 0 until the native content-height poll reports readiness. The poll can run for roughly one second, with a 2.5-second reveal failsafe, which can add perceived latency even after content has arrived.

Files:

- `core/data/.../MailRepository.kt` around `openEmailImap`, `openMessage`, and `prefetchInboxBodies`
- `core/data/.../ImapMailService.kt` around `withSession` and `fetchSource`
- `core/data/.../BodyCacheUpgrade.kt`
- `app/.../message/MessageScreen.kt` around `BODY_REVEAL_FAILSAFE_MS` and the content-height poll

### Expected behavior

Opening a message should become visibly responsive quickly. If the server or pooled IMAP session is stale, the operation should fail/reconnect within a bounded time rather than making the reader appear stuck.

Possible directions:

1. Add a finite wall-clock budget to foreground `fetchSource` calls and validate/reconnect stale pooled sessions.
2. Prefetch a small bounded number of recent IMAP message bodies.
3. Consider revealing the WebView at first usable paint rather than waiting for the final stable content height, while keeping the existing reflow protection.
4. Add stage timing around cache lookup, IMAP connect/select/fetch, MIME parse, and WebView reveal to distinguish the dominant delay.

I have not yet retested on 1.4.9. Its release notes do not mention message-open performance, and the paths above are still present in current source.

**Describe the bug**

Hi,

This regression is similar to the already fixed https://codeberg.org/OpenTracksApp/OpenTracks/issues/2317 / https://codeberg.org/OpenTracksApp/OSMDashboard/issues/603 issue.

Updates for single tracks work, but if more than one track is selected, the selected tracks will show up as finished (saw finishing line symbol) and the active track does not update.

**To Reproduce**
1. start recording
2. select active recording and a second already finished track
3. press open map button (using OSMDashboard)
4. walk a bit and check if the track updates

This feature was useful when you wanted to use a previously recorded track as reference.

title: Internal barometer cannot be selected with Bluetooth disabled
body:
**Describe the bug**
On my Google Pixel 8 Pro running Android 16, the application fails to calculate and display the total elevation gain/loss.
During the recording, the elevation fields display dashes ("-"). Once the track is saved, the elevation gain/loss block is completely hidden/missing from the final "Statistics" tab.
However, the altitude graph (green line) is perfectly generated, meaning the app successfully records GPS altitude data but fails to process the barometer data required for the gain/loss statistics.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior :

1. Open OpenTracks.
2. Activate GPS, wait 10+ seconds, then start a recording.
3. Perform an activity with significant elevation changes (e.g. in my case, a 14km trail).
4. Observe the live stats : Elevation gain/loss shows "-".
5. Stop the recording and check the "Statistics" tab.
6. The elevation gain/loss fields are completely missing, but the altitude graph is displayed correctly.

**Expected behavior**
The app should successfully read the device's internal barometer, calculate the elevation gain and loss, and display these values both during the live recording and in the final statistics screen.

**Environment :**

- Device : Google Pixel 8 Pro
- OS : Android 16
- OpenTracks Version : 4.26.2 (the paid one from Google Play Store)

Troubleshooting already performed :
To rule out common Android 14+ restrictions, I have already verified the following :

- Battery Optimization : Set to "Unrestricted" for OpenTracks.
- Permissions : "Sensors" is explicitly granted.
- Initialization : Tried waiting 10+ seconds before pressing "Start" to allow the barometer to wake up, with no success.

**Technical Hypothesis (thanks to Gemini)**
It appears OpenTracks is either unable to access the SensorManager for TYPE_PRESSURE on this specific device/OS combination, or the sensor's initialization is blocked by Android 16's strict background rules despite the unrestricted battery settings.

title: Attempting to log in without network is still possible - request should be wrapped in network check
body: Perhaps wrapping is not the best way to go. Instead, any API call should be able to handle a null response. This way, the network calls are reduced and it avoids having to ping another server.

* faster builds

title: HTTP-Cover fetching isnt working properly with "%d" due to trailing '/' character
body:
By using the configuration "Use HTTP-Cover" with line "http://host/music_dir/%d" the request from M.A.L.P gets resolved to "http://host/music_dir/path%2Fto%2Ffile%2F/cover.png" which is equal to "http://host/music_dir/path/to/file//cover.png".
Notice the double '/' at the end. This causes an 404 Error.

In Line 100-102 or in 119 (functions setRegex/resolveRegex) is the "Bug" i think:

title: Option for setting actual cover art filename to fetch over HTTP
body:
Right now the HTTP cover art fetcher always seems to query 48 different filenames (cover/folder and jpg/jpeg/png in various upper/lower case combinations). All my cover art files are called "cover.jpg", so it would be nice if there was a way to tell MALP to look for this and only this name.

Maybe if a filename like cover.jpg is (optionally) given in the HTTP path, MALP should only try to fetch this file name?

title: Password doesn't work with certain special characters
body:
*Created by: mrjpaxton*

When I put an apostrophe in my MPD password, for example, then enter in my password in the "Password:" field in the profile entry, it will not connect. (And by the way, it returns no pop-up errors like "failed to connect", so I've been wondering what the heck was going on.)

So the expected result is that the password should work with special characters like the apostrophe, since it works just fine with ncmpcpp. When I removed the apostrophe from my password, it M.A.L.P worked correctly.

M.A.L.P so far is a clean UX and efficient MPD remote/streaming client, especially with that OLED theme, and I really look forward to future improvements!

Thank you very much for this piece of software.

title: MALP needs to escape more characters in release queries
body:
MALP sends requests like these:
http://musicbrainz.org/ws/2/release/?query=release:2006\-07\-07%3A%20Stadion%2C%20Stockholm%2C%20Sweden&limit=3&fmt=json

.. but the server returns "400 Unable to parse search:release:2006\-07\-07: Stadion, Stockholm, Sweden" because the colon is not escaped as expected by the server.

This request works:
http://musicbrainz.org/ws/2/release/?query=release:2006\-07\-07\%3A%20Stadion%2C%20Stockholm%2C%20Sweden&limit=3&fmt=json

In sufficiently large novels, the download function seems to not work.
While the app can still access the chapter online, some chapters will not download unless true-deleted (potentially multiple times)

1. Use RoyalRoad or Scribblehub (I have only really used these extensions, and the issue appears to exist on both, with scribblehub having the issue more often)

3. Click download all
4. Wait until notification states download finishing

When I click download all, I expect all chapters to be downloaded, not play some arduous game of "look for the chapters that don't have downloaded next to them and true-delete them"

title: Current auto-true-delete implementation in dev branch will mark new chapters as read in certain situations
body:
### Background ###
In my mind, the auto-true-delete feature has a few use cases:
1. If a chapter is saved or bookmarked, don't auto-delete the chapter regardless of the following
2. When one or more chapters are removed and no chapters are added, delete those chapters
3. When one or more chapters are removed and one or more chapters are added, delete the removed chapters and add the new chapters as unread
4. When a chapter is changed (title, link, text, etc), update the chapter while respecting the read/unread state

These use cases are, more or less, in priority order.  If a given implementation solves for a particular use case but fails on previous use cases, IMO it shouldn't be used.

### The Issue ###
```
val matchingChapter = dbChapters.find { it.url == newChapter.link }
  ?: dbChapters.find { it.order == newChapter.order }

```
The issue is, in my understanding, the current implementation ([ChaptersDao.kt line 99ish](../development/android/src/main/java/app/shosetsu/android/providers/database/dao/ChaptersDao.kt#L98-99)) solves use case 4 while failing on 3 - if a new chapter comes in (so it has a link that does not match existing links), and some chapters were deleted (so the order number of the new chapter matches that of a current chapter that may have been read), the new chapter will inherit the read state of the "current" (not actually matching) chapter.  This will I believe always be true if we try to match on order number, so I don't think we should go down that road.

### Proposed Solution ###
What I think we *should* do is parse chapter IDs for the sources that provide it.  This would at least solve for RoyalRoad, which I believe (and could easily be wrong here) is the primary offender for deleting chapters.  Some sources may not provide chapter IDs, in which case we could fall back on link or title, but we still shouldn't fall back on order number for the reasons above.

### Open Questions ###
Is there a reason Novel/Chapter ID aren't parsed at the moment?  Is that a thing I'm free to implement, or is there something that would screw up?

title: Negative and Zero Transactions Managed Incorrectly
body:
This covers the same fields with two different edge-case values.  When using a negative or zero price, there are unexpected results.

For negative values of transactions, this is accepted on the transaction page.  Simply enter "-1" on any coin and it will successfully store the transaction.  This could be a desired feature (people wanting to enter sell dates, partial sells, then buys at different prices, etc), which is great.  Another random use, for instance, I wanted to enter fees in which is another needed feature, but since the feature isn't available opted to enter negative Tether values since Tether stays at a constant $1.  After having a negative overall asset value (or just a single negative transaction?) the portfolio page shows up, but when tapping the coin the coin specific asset page crashes the application entirely.  The UI just seems to hang/crash, and you have to kill the app and restart it.  Everything stays working after restart, no damage to data.

Also, "0.0" or "0" are a valid transaction "purchase" values for a coin on a portfolio you wish to track.  If you receive donations or receive a payment for goods in person, for instance.  The way the UI reacts is just to prevent the transaction from being stored entirely saying "Please enter a valid number".

Thanks for the hard work, this is a great project :)

title: Duplicate messages fetched in the background on Android
body:
_Created by [emersion](https://todo.sr.ht/~emersion) on 2024-05-10 11:19:17_

This has been going on for a while, just opening this for tracking and future reference.

Sometimes goguma will show duplicate messages. This looks like:

```
21:35 <emersion> foo
21:35 <emersion> foo
21:35 <emersion> foo
21:42 <emersion> bar
21:42 <emersion> bar
21:42 <emersion> bar
```

The repetition number varies, usually between 2 and 5. Only happens on Android, pretty randomly. For me it's more frequent with a spotty network and when leaving the phone idle for a long time.

I've tried reproducing in the Android emulator, simulating a TCP RST on the soju side, simulating a cellular network disconnection, killing the app in the background, to no avail.

This can't be a chathistory timestamp precision issue (due to second granularity), because the repetition happens with messages with a completely different timestamp fetched in the same batch.

Originally I thought this was a bug in our chathistory logic (timestamp not bumped in commands), or in our reconnection logic (resulting in multiple sockets opened at the same time), but after reading the code over and over again in the past year or so I couldn't find anything amiss.

Without `no-implicit-names`, detailed per-channel WHO information is never fetched because it's guarded behind `if (buffer.members == null)`.

title: Disconnect individual clients right after synchronization
body:
_Created by [emersion](https://todo.sr.ht/~emersion) on 2024-02-10 14:07:36_

Currently, `_handleWorkManagerSync()` waits for `_syncChatHistory()` to be completely done with all networks before disconnecting clients. Instead, we should disconnect each client right after it's done synchronizing, to avoid receiving regular messages.

This won't stop us from receiving regular messages during synchornization though. Maybe we should have a special `Client` or `ClientProvider` mode where regular messages are ignored.

title: Map downloader shows size of large files as -1
body:
*Created by: mvglasow*

The offline map downloader shows -1 for the size of some map files. This has been observed for the map of France, which is 2.2G in size (as of 2017-08-18, which is the most recent version).

Deeper analysis of the code shows that `HttpDownloader.getFileInfo()` uses `java.net.URLConnection.getContentLength()` to get the file size. According to its javadoc, this method returns -1 if content length is not supplied or cannot be represented as a 32-bit integer (i.e. anything over 2 GiB).

title: Hide satellites with invalid azimuth/elevation
body:
*Created by: mvglasow*

Under certain circumstances satellites appear at the tip of the compass arrow in the sky plot, i.e. azimuth and elevation of 0°. These are most likely satellites for which ephemeris is not available, so check for hasEphemeris() and  display only satellites for which true is returned.

title: Gadgetbridge sync is skipping a day for sun/moon rise/set times
body:
Hello,

When enabling the support for Gadgetbridge, the sun rise, sun set, moon rise, and moon set times seem to be missing a day. This can be seen in Gadgetbridge by showing the cached weather data through the debug menu. It is not present in the TinyWeatherForecast logs.

The today data shows:
```
Sun Rise: 2024-02-01T08:16:48+0100
Sun Set: 2024-02-01T17:25:15+0100
Moon Rise: 2024-02-01T00:00:00+0100
Moon Set: 2024-02-01T10:31:07+0100
```

The data for day 0 (from the 24h forecasts) shows:
```
Sun Rise: 2024-02-03T08:13:41+0100
Sun Set: 2024-02-03T17:28:53+0100
Moon Rise: 2024-02-03T02:12:29+0100
Moon Set: 2024-02-03T10:58:29+0100
```

`2024-02-02` is missing. After that it does have the data for every day.

The min/max temperatures and humidity for day 0 match up with the values for 2024-02-02, so those are correct.

Thank you for the great app!


Edit: I forgot to add the version I'm on: 0.61.4 from f-droid.

title: Panic Migration Onboarding shows up without migration
body:
The idea of the panic migration onboarding was that we show this only on migrations to explain the changes to users.

However, if you set up a fresh 2.0 install, then go to panic settings, connect ripple and activate app hiding, then on next start of the app, the onboarding will be shown, even though the user never was on 1.x.

title: Panic - broken if Exit app is not ON
body:
Nightly 2.0-rc1-985dba6e Android 17

Have Exit ON, Hide ON, trigger Panic, get Calculator :tada: 

Have Exit OFF, Hide ON, trigger Panic... nothing happens :shrug: 


In 1.xx Exit ON was a MUST for Panic actions, if you'd turned it OFF it would have turned Hide OFF too

Not sure this is needed or not now, I mean can we change the icon without exiting the app? My guess is not...

title: Prav app does not open after latest update on Google Play
body:
@ravidwivedi and I have been receiving reports of the Prav app not opening on Android after a recent update.

I have not been able to test it personally as I use Mobian and KaiOS, not Android, but most people describe the situation as "the app refuses to open". More information from those who use Google Play is welcome.

This issue is affecting users who install or update the app via Google Play. F-droid installations seem to be unaffected.

Initial reports were about the app refusing to open after upgrading to the latest version of Prav. However, @contrapunctus reported the same issues when trying to onboard new users, so it seems the issue is with the APK itself and not update related.

title: Check for internet connectivity before making a request to the website
body:
The app keeps trying to ping the websites even if the mobile isn't connected to the internet and marks them as 404 not found. This results in a lot of notifications that aren't related to the status of the website at all.

Suggestions:
1. Pause activity on all websites when network change is detected (internet on to off). Resume when device is connected again. OR
2. Check internet status before every request. 

This can be kept behind a settings option.

title: Reader mode doesn't show images
body:
## Summary

Opening an article in reader mode displays only blank squares instead of images. 

## Steps to reproduce

Add newsfeed.zeit.de RSS feed and open an article. 

## What is the current bug behavior?

The article opens and displays text but instead of images there are only blank squares. 

## What is the expected correct behavior?

The opened article should also display images. 

## Relevant logs and/or screenshots

![Screenshot_20240708-004355](/uploads/c4d0f1231c6870eb2ad0dc60fe9621ca/Screenshot_20240708-004355.png)

## Android version, Nunti version and device info

Android 10  
Nunti from F-Droid v2.5.2  
Sony Xperia XZ3 (H8416)  

## Possible fixes

No idea, HTML gets pulled in `WebpageParser` and sanitized using `sanitize-html`. Allowed tags include `img`, so this one probably works correctly.   
Then parsed using `DOMParser`, which probably doesn't care so probably doesn't break images either.  
Then `Readibility` parses it, this might break images of course, it's probably hard to check this without debugging.  
Then that gets put into articleContent of the view, no idea if that even has settings to do anything about images.

Never touched react native so I'm not a great help with UI things I guess.

title: Reader mode also used for issue tracker
body:
## Summary

When using reader mode, opening the issues tracker opens it in reader mode, which of course doesn't work at all for Gitlab. 

## Steps to reproduce

- go to settings
- set browser mode to reader mode
- go to about
- open issue tracker

## What is the current bug behavior?

Gitlab is shown in reader mode. 

## What is the expected correct behavior?

Gitlab should be opened in webview or external browser to facilitate interactivity. 

## Relevant logs and/or screenshots

![Screenshot_20240708-005654](/uploads/7c4cca58006c2e9fea5c60dbea59af71/Screenshot_20240708-005654.png)

## Android version, Nunti version and device info

Android 10  
Nunti from F-Droid, v2.5.2  
H8416

## Possible fixes

https://gitlab.com/ondrejfoltyn/nunti/-/blob/master/Nunti/src/Screens/About.tsx#L70 uses the same `openBrowser` method that opens depending on user setting. 

- There could be an override parameter that makes sure no integrated reader is used
- There could be a different method so this call explicitly opens a webview or external browser, regardless of user setting
- Opening an article could instead call a `readArticle` that either opens the internal reader or calls `openBrowser` so `openBrowser` would only ever open a browser, maybe use webview as a default for reader mode or default case

No idea which of these fit best for your architecture though.

title: A lot of common sensors aren't supported because of temperature and humidity error
body:
Your Feinstaubwidget doesn't display temperature and humidity if sensor type is BME280. This sensor is compatible to DHT11/DHT22 and additionally measures air pressure. Your Widget should support this sensor because it's often used.

See difference between DHT11/DHT22 and BME280:

DHT22:  http://api.luftdaten.info/v1/sensor/1315/  
BME280: http://api.luftdaten.info/v1/sensor/15662/

None of your JSON parsers works with BME280. I don't understand your concept of different parsers - one parser should be enough. For my own software I used the free libjansson which is part of Linux, easy to use and available for all operation systems incl. Android. https://jansson.readthedocs.io/en/2.10/gettingstarted.html

BTW: My parser routine C/C++ for array of 'sensordatavalues' looks like this:

... array = json_array_get(sensordatavalues, i) ...
... if (json_unpack_ex(array, &error, 0, "{s:s,s:o,s?I*}", "value_type", &sensor[i].type, "value", &value, "id", &sensor[i].id)...

No regex required and order doesn't matter

progress bar then crawls extremely slowly, taking 10+ minutes to reach 100%,
and once it hits 100% the login fails with "you didn't pass the challenge."
The solved captcha token appears to be rejected. I cannot complete login and
therefore cannot receive notifications.

## Environment
- App version: latest F-Droid release (also reproduced with the direct build;
  behavior is identical between them)
- Install source: F-Droid
- OS: GrapheneOS (current release)
- Android System WebView: installed and up to date
- Google Play: sandboxed Google Play Services present in the same profile
- Network: fast, stable connection; reproduced on both Wi-Fi and mobile data
- VPN: none

## Steps to reproduce
1. Add a Proton Mail account in the app.
2. Login triggers the "Human Verification" screen (drag-the-puzzle-piece captcha).
3. The puzzle image renders correctly and I solve it.
4. "Verifying if you are human..." begins, but the progress bar advances
   extremely slowly — it takes 10+ minutes to crawl to 100%.
5. Once it reaches 100%, login fails with "you didn't pass the challenge."

## Expected behavior
After solving the captcha, verification should complete within seconds and the
account should be added.

## Actual behavior
The verification progress bar takes 10+ minutes to reach 100%, then the
challenge is rejected and login fails.

## What I've already tried (no effect)
- Repeatedly logging into account.proton.me in a desktop browser, solving the
  captcha there successfully, then immediately logging into the app on the same
  network. App still fails at the captcha.
- Both with 2FA enabled and disabled — the captcha is triggered regardless of 2FA.
- Multiple networks (home Wi-Fi and mobile data), no VPN. The 10+ minute delay
  and failure occur on all of them, so this is not a slow-connection issue.
- Reinstalling with the latest build.
- Confirmed the official Proton Mail app logs in and works fine on the same
  device, so account credentials, network, and WebView are all known-good.

## Notes / suspected cause
- The extremely slow progress (10+ minutes to reach 100%) suggests the
  verification round-trip is stalling/retrying internally rather than failing
  fast, before the token is ultimately rejected.
- This looks like the app's handling of Proton's current human-verification flow
  (visual challenge + proof-of-work "Proton CAPTCHA"). The solved token appears
  to be rejected by Proton's verification endpoint rather than simply expiring.
- Possibly a recent change to Proton's captcha/verification API, a mismatch in
  the API entry point used for submitting the verification token, or the
  proof-of-work step spinning for a very long time before submission.

## Willing to help
I'm happy to gather any logs or test debug builds, but I'm not the most knowledgeable about how to do any of that — I don't know how to capture logcat, run adb, etc. If you walk me through it step by step, assuming no prior knowledge, I'll follow it exactly.

title: Not completely deleting EXIF data: use library instead of ExifInterface
body:
Thanks to a user report:

```
Scrambled Exif doesn't delete the whole fields, only the data within them.

For example, this:
Camera make = "Example make"
Camera model = "Example model"

... turns into this:
Camera make = ""
Camera model = ""

... when it should delete everything, including the "Camera make" and "Camera model" fields.

This can be used to determine if the image was stripped with Scrambled Exif, and even the phone manufacturer and model, depending on the fields.
```

title: Only remove EXIF data from jpeg images
body:
Currently, Scrambled Exif accepts everything (image/*). Since it's using ExifInterface to delete the data, I think it probably doesn't have any effect on PNG metadata (which apparently exists).

Since I am not sure how to handle the png metadata, I am going to stop processing these. I think the most transparent way to handle this is to accept them anyway in the Intent (so combinations of pngs and jpegs will be accepted) and not to process the png files (including not offering them in the share dialog) and show a toast telling the user that these files can't be handled.
